bread-wheat-or-cracked-wheat-reduced-cal.title: Bread, wheat or cracked wheat, reduced calorie and/or high fiber, toasted

content.title: About
content.content: This is a whole‑grain bread made from whole wheat or cracked wheat, formulated to be lower in calories and higher in dietary fiber. The loaf is toasted to a golden crust, giving it a crunchy texture and a rich aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Toasting enhances flavor and creates a crisp crust while preserving most nutrients.
Wheat is one of the oldest cultivated crops, grown by humans for over 10,000 years.
High fiber content helps regulate blood sugar and supports digestive health.
Reduced calories are achieved by lowering fat content and using a lighter recipe.
Traditional stone‑oven baking retains the natural taste of the grain.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion, increases satiety, and can help lower cholesterol levels.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: Fewer calories make this bread suitable for energy‑restricted diets.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Complex carbohydrates provide steady energy release and support stable blood glucose.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Wheat supplies thiamine, riboflavin, and niacin, which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The bread contains magnesium, phosphorus, and iron, important for bone health and blood formation.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: People with celiac disease or gluten intolerance may experience serious reactions.

items.title: Gluten content
items.content: The product contains gluten and is not suitable for a gluten‑free diet.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Toasted bread can have higher sodium; individuals with hypertension should monitor portion size.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The bread works well for toast, sandwiches, soup accompaniments, and as a base for open‑face toppings. Pair it with low‑fat cheese, vegetable spreads, avocado, or cottage cheese.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bread in a cool, dry place in a paper bag or container to keep the crust crisp. For longer storage, freeze it and toast slices before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: Greens are edible leafy vegetables such as spinach, kale, lettuce, Swiss chard and others. In this product they are served fresh, steamed or blanched without any added fat, preserving the maximum amount of nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Greens are rich in chlorophyll, which gives them their bright green color and has antioxidant properties.
Some greens, like spinach, contain oxalates that can affect calcium absorption.
Steaming retains up to 90 % of vitamins, whereas boiling in large amounts of water can reduce them.
Leafy greens are staples in many world cuisines: wasabi and seaweed in Japan, arugula in Italy, sorrel in Russia.

items.title: Rich source of vitamins
items.content: Greens provide vitamins A, C, K and B‑complex, supporting immunity, vision and blood clotting.

items.title: High mineral content
items.content: They contain iron, calcium, magnesium and potassium, essential for bones, muscles and nerves.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: A serving of greens contains fewer than 20 kcal, making them ideal for weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Phytonutrients such as lutein and zeaxanthin help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber in greens promotes intestinal motility and a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Oxalates
items.content: High intake of oxalates may contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: If not washed properly, greens may retain traces of agricultural chemicals.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Rarely, some people may be allergic to specific leafy vegetables.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Greens can be eaten raw in salads, added to smoothies, steamed, blanched, or used as a side dish. Cooking without added fat retains their natural flavor and nutritional profile.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store greens in the refrigerator in an airtight container or a bag with a small amount of moisture. Use within 2–3 days to prevent wilting.
